title: EU AI Act classification (per built product)
description: docs/compliance/ai-act.json in a target repo (chief-wiggum#316): one record per AI FEATURE, not per product. Produced by /architect, checked report-only by scripts/check_ai_act.py. Decoupled from docs/compliance-requirements.md (the regulated-DATA trigger) — this artifact triggers on AI FUNCTIONALITY and market reach, per the Act's own hook. Its own presence/absence is a legal fact under Art. 6(4): a provider claiming an Annex III system is NOT high-risk must document that assessment BEFORE the system is placed on the market, so a MISSING file is never equivalent to a recorded 'not high risk' — check_ai_act.py's classification_status distinguishes them explicitly.

eu_scope.description: Territorial-scope determination (Art. 2(1)(a)/(c)) — never a silent absence.

eu_scope_reason.description: The Art. 2 limb relied on, in prose. TBD: markers gate dependent tickets via check_unresolved.py.

features.description: One entry per AI feature (a chat assistant, a recommendation engine, an emotion-inference component, ...) — NOT one entry per product. An empty array is a genuine, recorded 'this product has no AI features' (check_ai_act.py: classification_status=recorded, outcome=inapplicable) — different from the file not existing at all (classification_status=missing, outcome=findings).

role.description: Art. 25: putting your name on a system makes you its provider.

performs_profiling.description: Always required, always checked: profiling is ALWAYS high-risk and voids any Art. 6(3) derogation, regardless of the tier otherwise claimed.

derogation_assessment.description: Required when tier=high_risk_annex_iii and the feature is claimed NOT high-risk (Art. 6(4)) — the assessment document itself, not just a flag.

obligations.description: Article refs this feature owes, e.g. 'Art. 50(1)', 'Art. 50(2)'.

evidence.description: @cw-trace handles into code/tests/screenshots proving each obligation is actually wired — never a re-serialized contract body.

legal_signoff.description: TBD: markers for anything a lawyer must confirm before this record can be relied on.
